topics.topic: How credential-resolution failure during `service_invoker.prepare_request` must be surfaced (propagated refusal/error vs prepare_request failure result detail)
questions: How must a credential-resolution failure be surfaced by prepare_request: as a prepare_request result detail or as a propagated refusal/error?

When credential resolution fails during request preparation, is it a refusal from `installation.resolve_service_credential` or a non-refusal pre-send failure result returned by `service_invoker.prepare_request`?

quotes:
One prepared request — carrying the binding's output Ports for A09 rule 3 — its
description of A10 rule 7 and its `request_digest`; or the first pre-send
failure — a credential `installation` cannot resolve becomes
`credential_unresolved` here.
judgement.why: The text explicitly states that credential-resolution failure is surfaced by `prepare_request` as a pre-send failure detail, not as a propagated refusal.
judgement.failure: the answering quote is not found verbatim in the texts

topics.topic: `store.read_records`: whether malformed relation arguments are part of the public error contract (e.g., `internal_error`) or out of scope/impossible
questions: Must store.read_records return internal_error for malformed relation arguments as part of its public API, in addition to unknown_reference?
For `store.read_records`, are malformed relation arguments (wrong/missing/extra) a defined `internal_error` outcome, or are such calls impossible and therefore out of scope of the operation contract?

quotes:
A call that passes other arguments is a defect of its caller and
answers `internal_error` — so does one that omits an argument its relation
names or passes one of another kind; that defect is decided before any record
is looked up.
judgement.why: The contract explicitly defines malformed relation arguments as an `internal_error` outcome.

topics.topic: JCS canonicalization failure at MCP ingress: whether `surface` remaps to `invalid_request` or `canonical_bytes` returns `invalid_request` directly
questions: When JCS canonicalization fails at request ingress, must `surface` remap that failure to `invalid_request`, or should `canonical_bytes` itself use `invalid_request` in this path?

questions: Which exact service set must be iterated for this start check (all services mentioned anywhere in installation, only services with selected instances, only services with credentials, or another set)?

questions: If a candidate value contains a non-finite number (e.g. NaN/Inf) outside MCP ingress (for example from sandbox output), which failure should `fit_port_value` return, and at which check position?

questions: When this specific relation finds no FlowActivation, should store.read_records return empty or internal_error?
